title: Cloudflare Introduces Web Search API for AI Applications
gist: Cloudflare launched a beta Web Search API via AI Gateway, routing agent searches to Ceramic.ai, Exa and Linkup with unified logging, billing and BYO keys at list price, while requiring providers to meet verified-bot rules and return source links. Commentators see Cloudflare edging toward 'main cloud supplier' status, while data-retention and resyndication terms remain key concerns.

themes.theme: Cloudflare as AI agent infrastructure layer

insights.claim: Cloudflare launched a beta Web Search API through AI Gateway, available via REST and Workers, that unifies logging, access control and billing for search providers Ceramic.ai, Exa and Linkup and supports bring-your-own-provider keys.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is aggregating agent tool calls, not just model inference, through its gateway.

insights.claim: Cloudflare offers search at providers' list prices without markup and plans to add native server tools to AI Gateway, starting with web search.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Zero-markup pricing suggests a land-grab for agent traffic and billing share.
insights.quote: offers search at providers’ list prices without additional markup

insights.claim: Maximilian Goisser argues Cloudflare is approaching the status of a trusted main cloud supplier, alongside AWS, GCP and Azure, through which most cloud costs are billed, avoiding fresh procurement.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Billing consolidation is a moat; Cloudflare is encroaching on hyperscaler wallet share.
insights.quote: I think Cloudflare is (for companies already using it) approaching the status of trusted main cloud supplier

themes.theme: Agent web access and the 'fair Internet' rules

insights.claim: Cloudflare says agents fetching live pages often guess URLs and curl them, producing 404 errors, which is inefficient and motivates a proper search API.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Agent web retrieval is a real inefficiency creating demand for search APIs.
insights.quote: the agent usually just guesses the URL of the page and then makes a tool call to curl it

insights.claim: Search providers on Cloudflare's API must comply with its Verified Bots requirements and include links to crawled content, which Cloudflare frames as letting creators decide how their data is used.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is using its network position to set terms of AI crawling.
insights.quote: These rules are net-positive for a fair Internet, and allow creators to decide what they want to do with their data.

themes.theme: Search API terms as a constraint

insights.claim: Simon Willison argues the key question about search APIs is whether results can be stored and resyndicated, since forbidding storage or transcript sharing significantly limits agent systems, and the answer is usually buried in terms.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Data-retention licensing, not search quality alone, may determine which search APIs win agent workloads.
insights.quote: My number one question about search APIs is always if they allow you to store and resyndicate results you get from them.

insights.claim: Cloudflare says it will identify which search providers support Zero Data Retention.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: ZDR is becoming a procurement checkbox for enterprise agent tooling.
